title: DROP PROCEDURE
description: DROP PROCEDURE removes a procedure definition - like DROP FUNCTION, you need the parameter types since procedures can be overloaded too. The fixtures already include a procedure `mark_appointment_completed(appointment_id INTEGER)` - drop it.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: DROP PROCEDURE
DROP PROCEDURE <name>(<param_type>) - same idea as DROP FUNCTION, just the PROCEDURE keyword and this procedure's own single-parameter signature.
Use DROP PROCEDURE followed by mark_appointment_completed and the exact parameter type (INTEGER) in parentheses.
expected_behavior: mark_appointment_completed(INTEGER) no longer exists as a procedure.
explanation: Just like DROP FUNCTION, this needs the full parameter signature because Postgres allows more than one procedure to share the same name as long as their parameter types differ.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'mark_appointment_completed' AND pronamespace = 'fixtures'::regnamespace
hidden_tests.label: mark_appointment_completed procedure is gone
